integration_questions: With wheel_track at 0.10 m, which kp and kd range was stable, and did the robot oscillate or overshoot on the oval?
Does max_error still peak at the same point on the s-bend and slalom, and is line loss at that point?
Did the narrower track change the control effort needed for the same bend, compared with the 0.12 m track?
Which sensors carry most of the signal, and can the outer sensors be given smaller weights to reduce line loss?
feedback_request.requested_format: Brief notes on each question, plus the single geometry change you would make first if you could change only one thing.

intent: Isolate the wheel-track effect by reverting to the iteration 1 layout (7 sensors at 0.02 m spacing spanning 0.12 m, 16 mm footprints, y = 0.06 m, mass 0.6 kg) and changing only wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. Expect more yaw per PWM unit, fewer off-track ends on the s-bend and slalom, and a score at or above 482.7. Keep wheel radius and body size fixed so the change is attributable.
learning: Iteration 2 suggests the wider 0.15 m span or the lower mass or the forward lead was harmful, since the score fell when all four changed. Hypotheses to test: (1) a 0.10 m track gives enough extra turn authority to cut s-bend off-track ends; (2) the 0.15 m span spreads sensor resolution too thin, so the 0.12 m span is better; (3) the iteration 2 mass and lead changes did not help. Measurements to request on each development track: completion, progress, completion_time, max_error, rms_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort.
rationale: Iteration 1 (score 482.7) is the best design so far. Iteration 2 changed span (0.12 to 0.15 m), wheel track (0.12 to 0.10 m), mass (0.6 to 0.5 kg) and sensor lead (0.06 to 0.07 m) together, and the score fell to 411.7. The s-bend completion rate dropped from 5/20 to 0/20, and the slalom still never finished. The oval was unchanged at 20/20 finishes. Every failure is an off-track end with max_error at or above 0.06 m, while rms_error stays small (0.022 to 0.030 m). So the limit is occasional large excursions on bends, not steady tracking error. Body width cannot widen the off-track limit, because max(0.06, 0.0125 + width/4) stays at 0.06 m across the allowed range. Iteration 2 is confounded, so I cannot tell which of its four changes hurt. I will revert to the iteration 1 design and change only one variable: wheel track from 0.12 to 0.10 m. This is a clean test of whether more turn authority per PWM unit (turn rate scales with wheel-speed difference divided by track) reduces bend excursions. If the score rises above 482.7, the track is the lever and the span was the harm in iteration 2. If it falls, the track is not the lever, and the span widening is the likely cause. Expected result: s-bend completions at or above the iteration 1 rate, with max_error below 0.06 m on more runs. Main risk: the narrower track may increase oscillation at speed on the oval.
